new.title: Visit the Friedenssaal where the Peace of Westphalia was signed
new.desc: The late Gothic Rathaus on the Markt hosted the Osnabrück half of the 1648 Westphalian peace negotiations. Its Friedenssaal still holds portraits of the envoys and carved panelling.
new.tip: Guided tours and the Friedenssaal are usually available on weekdays and Saturdays; check opening hours first.
new.q: Rathaus des Westfälischen Friedens, Markt 30, Osnabrück

new.title: Step into the Dom St. Peter and its cloister
new.desc: Osnabrück's cathedral dates mainly from the 13th century and mixes Romanesque and Gothic architecture. The adjoining cloister and cathedral treasury add to a visit.
new.tip: Entry to the church is free; the treasury has separate hours.

new.title: Admire the Gothic Marienkirche on the market square
new.desc: A 14th-century Gothic hall church that stands at the Markt beside the Rathaus and Stadtwaage. Its tower can be climbed as part of a guided tour.
new.tip: Ask the tourist information about tower tours.

new.title: Look at the Stadtwaage and the stepped gables of the Markt
new.desc: The Markt is framed by the Rathaus, the Marienkirche, the Stadtwaage and stepped-gable houses. The square hosts events such as the Maiwoche.
new.tip: Come on a market day for the busiest atmosphere.

new.title: Walk through the Heger Tor, the Waterloo gate
new.desc: The classicist city gate commemorates the Osnabrück soldiers who fell at Waterloo in 1815, hence its second name. It marks the entrance to the lively Heger-Tor quarter.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll into the old town through Heger Straße.

new.title: Find the medieval Bucksturm tower
new.desc: A 13th-century tower on Bocksmauer Straße that survives from the medieval city wall. It is a listed monument in the old town.
new.tip: Best seen on a walk along the former wall line.

new.title: Explore the Felix-Nussbaum-Haus by Daniel Libeskind
new.desc: Opened in 1998, the museum designed by Daniel Libeskind holds the world's largest collection of works by Osnabrück-born Jewish painter Felix Nussbaum. It forms part of the Museumsquartier MQ4.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; check the official hours before you go.

new.title: See the Kulturgeschichtliches Museum in the MQ4
new.desc: The city's museum of cultural history sits in the Museumsquartier next to the Felix-Nussbaum-Haus and covers Osnabrück and the region from early times to the present.
new.tip: Pairs well with a visit to the Nussbaum museum.

new.title: Visit Die Villa_, the former Villa Schlikker
new.desc: This villa in the Museumsquartier was the NSDAP district headquarters between 1933 and 1945. Today it serves as a place for history education within MQ4.
new.tip: Check current exhibitions on the MQ4 website.

new.title: See contemporary art in the Kunsthalle Dominikanerkirche
new.desc: The Kunsthalle occupies the former church of the Dominican monastery of the Holy Cross. Temporary exhibitions of contemporary art are shown inside the medieval nave.
new.tip: Exhibitions change, so check the programme first.

new.title: Stroll around Schloss Osnabrück and its garden
new.desc: The former prince-bishop's residence was built from 1667 and now houses the University of Osnabrück. The Schlossgarten lies behind it.
new.tip: The garden is open to everyone.

new.title: Spot the Renaissance Ledenhof near the cathedral
new.desc: A Renaissance mansion owned by the city since 1930 and used for the Deutsche Stiftung Friedensforschung and the Literaturbüro Westniedersachsen.
new.tip: Admire the exterior on an old-town walk.

new.title: Wander the Botanischer Garten in the Westerberg quarries
new.desc: The university's botanical garden lies in two former quarries on the Westerberg. Entry is free and themed guided tours are available on request.
new.tip: Combine with a walk on the Westerberg.
new.q: Botanischer Garten der Universität Osnabrück, Albrechtstraße 29, Osnabrück

new.title: Dig into coal-mining history at the Museum Industriekultur
new.desc: The museum on the Piesberg tells the story of the area's coal mining and industrial heritage. It sits within the Piesberg cultural landscape.
new.tip: Pair with the Piesberg viewing platform.

new.title: Discover nature at the Museum am Schölerberg
new.desc: A municipal museum for nature and the environment next to the zoo at the Schölerberg, with hands-on exhibits.
new.tip: Combine with the zoo visit.

new.title: Walk the Hexengang by the cathedral
new.desc: A historic lane by the Dom where plague victims once prayed during services, warning others with wooden clappers.
new.tip: Short stop on the old-town walk.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Hausbrauerei Rampendahl
new.desc: A home brewery on Hasestraße serving three of its own beers with hearty traditional German meat dishes.
new.tip: Opens evenings on weekdays and from 11:00 on Friday to Sunday, so check first.

new.title: Have coffee and cake at Café am Markt
new.desc: A traditional café on the market square with chandeliers and Art Nouveau-style furnishings.
new.tip: Ask for a window seat facing the Rathaus.

new.title: Taste roasted coffee at Barösta Kaffeehaus
new.desc: A café on Redlinger Straße that has operated since 2012, with its own small roastery added in 2014.
new.tip: Take beans home from the roastery.

new.title: Dine in the historic Walhalla on Bierstraße
new.desc: The Romantik Hotel Walhalla claims to be the city's oldest inn and offers German and French dishes in a timber-framed building. Erich Maria Remarque set parts of The Black Obelisk here.
new.tip: Book ahead for dinner.

new.title: Raise a glass in the Olle Use, a 1608 town house pub
new.desc: The oldest pub in the city occupies a 1608 town house belonging to the Walhalla.
new.tip: Good for an evening drink in the old town.

new.title: Eat a flexible bistro meal at Henne Cafébar
new.desc: A bistro, café and restaurant on Osterberger Reihe with vegetarian and vegan options.
new.tip: Good for brunch or a relaxed dinner.

new.title: Spend a day at Zoo Osnabrück
new.desc: Opened in 1936 on the Schölerberg, the zoo keeps more than 2,600 animals of about 290 species in twelve themed worlds, including an underground section.
new.tip: Allow a full day; summer weekends are busiest.

new.title: Surf the standing wave at Hasewelle
new.desc: An artificial surf wave at the L&T Sporthaus on Große Straße. Sessions last 45 minutes for up to ten people with board, wetsuit and helmet included.
new.tip: Minimum age 8; book ahead and check current slots.

new.title: Slide and swim at the Nettebad
new.desc: The leisure pool has a 50 metre sports pool, a large slide landscape and a sauna area.
new.tip: Check hours and prices before visiting.

new.title: Rent a pedal boat on the Rubbenbruchsee
new.desc: This lake in the city offers pedal boats for hire, plus lakeside paths and swimming.
new.tip: Best on summer weekends.

new.title: Stroll Hasestraße, the old trade route
new.desc: Described as Osnabrück's oldest trade route, running from the cathedral toward the old station, lined with restaurants and a brewery.
new.tip: Walk it in the evening and stop at Rampendahl.

new.title: Follow the Haseuferweg along the river
new.desc: A riverside path running through the city from the station bridge to the Hasetor.
new.tip: Share the path with cyclists.

new.title: Climb to the Piesberg landscape park viewpoint
new.desc: The Piesberg cultural and landscape park spans about 300 million years of earth history and has a viewing platform.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes.

new.title: Wander the Heger-Tor quarter
new.desc: The quarter around the Heger Tor is known for narrow streets, small shops and restaurants and is a good place for an evening out.
new.tip: Start at the gate and head into Heger Straße.
